hypothesis: In 3D-segmented plant tissue (ovule and lateral-root cells), cell-wall junctions where three cells meet have mean dihedral/planar angles near 120°, and the deviation from 120° is not correlated with the size difference of the neighbouring cells.
pass_criterion: Using ≥1000 triple-cell junctions measured in 2D reslices of the ground-truth label stacks, the mean interwall angle lies within 120° ± 5°, the circular SD is ≤ 20°, and the Spearman correlation between a junction's deviation from 120° and the log volume ratio of its largest to smallest adjacent cell is |rho| < 0.2.
fail_criterion: Mean junction angle outside 120° ± 5° (e.g. <115° or >125°), or SD > 20°, or |rho| ≥ 0.3 between angle deviation and neighbour size ratio, indicating angles depend on cell size.
interpretation: 'Cell-walls meeting by threes' means edges of the wall network where exactly three cell labels meet in a planar section (or three wall sheets meet along a line in 3D). 'Angle' is the angle between tangents of the wall segments at the junction, estimated within a small radius (~2 µm) to avoid curvature bias. 'Size of cells' is label volume (or 2D area). Modern reinterpretation: Thompson's soap-froth analogy is for minimal-surface equilibrium; real plant walls resist turgor and growth, so deviations are expected and a tolerance is pre-set. Ground-truth segmentations are hand-curated, which may bias toward smooth walls.

dataset.name: Accurate and versatile 3D segmentation of plant tissues at cellular resolution: Core Datasets
dataset.publisher: Open Science Framework (Wolny et al., PlantSeg; EMBL/Heidelberg)
dataset.why_it_fits: Contains confocal Arabidopsis ovule and light-sheet lateral-root stacks with hand-curated ground-truth cell instance labels (48 volumes), from which triple junctions, wall angles and per-cell volumes can be computed. Files are listed at https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/uzq3w/files/; fields used: raw image, ground-truth label volumes.
